passages.label: A
passages.heading: Subject: Thursday client visit — revised start time
passages.body:
Dear Jordan,

Thank you for confirming that Ms. Alvarez will visit our downtown showroom on Thursday. Because of a delayed flight, she will now arrive at 11:15 a.m. instead of 10:00 a.m.

Please meet her at the reception desk and escort her to Meeting Room 3. I have reserved the room until 1:00 p.m. and arranged a light lunch for three people.

If the product samples from the warehouse are not ready by 10:30 a.m., call me so we can adjust the presentation order. Otherwise, begin with the new catalog overview as planned.

Best regards,
Nora Kim
Account Lead, BrightPath Interiors

questions.question: What time is Ms. Alvarez now expected to arrive?
questions.explanation: The email states she will now arrive at 11:15 a.m. instead of 10:00 a.m. because of a delayed flight.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing 10:00 a.m. — that was the original time, not the revised one.

questions.question: What can be inferred about Meeting Room 3?

options.text: It is located in the warehouse.
It has been reserved for the client visit.
It will be unavailable until 1:00 p.m.
It is where product samples are stored.

questions.correctAnswer: It has been reserved for the client visit.
questions.explanation: Nora writes that she has reserved Meeting Room 3 until 1:00 p.m. for the visit. The other options are not supported.
questions.commonMistake: Misreading “reserved until 1:00 p.m.” as meaning the room is unavailable until then.

questions.question: In the email, the word “escort” is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: Jordan is asked to meet Ms. Alvarez at reception and escort her to Meeting Room 3 — that is, go with her / accompany her there.
questions.commonMistake: Associating “escort” only with security or formal events and missing the workplace sense of guiding a visitor.
